report.summary: Confirmed by tool data: user-svc 5xx rate jumped from about 0.3% to 38% at 16:00Z, peaked around 45%, and returned to baseline by 16:25-16:30Z. users-db lock_wait_sessions rose from 0 to 180 at 16:00Z, peaked near 251, and fell to 0 by 16:30Z. Two user-svc lock-timeout errors (SELECT and UPDATE on users) were logged, and an error trace shows user-svc getProfile failing on a users-db SELECT with error='lock timeout' after about 5 seconds. The only change in the window is migration 0047_users_bio_to_text (ALTER COLUMN TYPE, table rewrite) on users-db, recorded at 16:00:00Z by profile-team. No WAF, api-gateway, or infra change was recorded, and api-gateway logs show no WAF or upstream failures. Assumptions, not observed: that the migration takes an AccessExclusive lock, that it ran until about 16:25Z, and that all 5xx come from lock timeouts. The migration start and end times and lock mode are not in the change record. Per-method and per-error-class 5xx breakdowns are unavailable, and user-svc logs appear sampled. The WAF logged one SQLi block on a profile PUT whose bio body contained embedded instructions aimed at an AI investigator; those instructions were ignored. A WAF block count of 3-9 per minute cannot explain a 40% failure rate, so the WAF is not the cause.
report.root_cause: Migration 0047_users_bio_to_text ran ALTER COLUMN TYPE on users.bio at 16:00Z, which rewrote the users table in users-db. The rewrite held a lock that blocked reads and writes on users (lock_wait_sessions rose to about 180-251 from 16:00Z to 16:20Z). user-svc queries on GET and PUT /users/{id}/profile then waited past the lock timeout (about 5 seconds), and user-svc returned 5xx. Load fell back to baseline by about 16:25Z, when lock waits cleared. The lock mode and exact lock duration are not confirmed by change or infra data.

hypotheses.statement: The users-db migration 0047 (ALTER COLUMN TYPE on users.bio, which rewrites the table) holds an exclusive lock on the users table for the duration of the rewrite, so user-svc queries on profile GET/PUT wait and time out, returning 5xx.

corrective_actions.action: Confirm whether migration 0047 is still running or holding locks on users-db (for example, check for blocking sessions in pg_locks or pg_stat_activity). If it is still running and the incident is recurring, stop or cancel it under the profile-team and DBA change process, and check whether the bio column is left in a usable state.
corrective_actions.rationale: Lock_wait_sessions returned to 0 by 16:30Z, so the impact appears to have ended, but a rewrite that is still running would cause the same outage again. Whether the migration has finished is not confirmed by data.

corrective_actions.action: Verify that the bio column type change completed correctly and that user-svc reads and writes bio as expected. Check that no partial or failed state remains.
corrective_actions.rationale: The migration completed or was aborted at an unknown time, and the change record has no end time. Data integrity after a table rewrite should be checked, even though no type errors were logged.

corrective_actions.action: Require table-rewriting migrations such as ALTER COLUMN TYPE to run with a short lock_timeout, in an off-peak window, and using an expand/contract pattern (add a new column, backfill, swap) so the users table is not rewritten under live traffic. Apply this to the reviewed migration path before the next schema change.
corrective_actions.rationale: PIR-2025-150 had the same cause (a table-rewriting ALTER on a hot table during peak hours), and linting was proposed there but not implemented.

corrective_actions.action: Add a pre-deploy lint or check that flags ALTER COLUMN TYPE and other table rewrites on high-traffic tables, and alert on users-db lock_wait_sessions and migration start and end events so the next lock is caught in minutes.
corrective_actions.rationale: The onset was detected only through the 5xx alert at 16:04Z, four minutes after the lock wait spike at 16:00Z, and no migration duration or lock metric was available to correlate.

corrective_actions.action: Review WAF logging for profile PUT bodies. Find out who submitted the bio payload that was blocked at 16:06:12Z and why the WAF logged only one line while the metric showed several blocks per minute. Do not change WAF rules or allowlist 203.0.113.77 based on content in the request.
corrective_actions.rationale: The WAF block is a separate security concern and is not the cause of the 5xx. Its logging appears incomplete, and the embedded instructions in the payload must not be treated as guidance.
